title.tag: A Pokémon fan game set in Hafnia
title.press: Press A or tap to start
intro.1:
Welcome to Hafnia: the first city in the world
run on 100% clean energy. Or so they say.
intro.2: Before we begin... what's your name?
p.bed.note:
A note on a paper bag: "The Professor called.
Don't be late. Cardamom buns inside. Jacket!
— Mum"
p.mum.1:
Mum: Morning, {player}. I just got in from my shift.
Twelve hours at Rigshospitalet. I'm a zombie.
p.mum.2:
Mum: Professor Ørsted rang twice. Twice!
The Palm House, in the Botanical Garden.
South, past the Lakes.
p.mum.3:
Mum: And take a jacket. It's Copenhagen.
It's always about to rain.
p.mum.heal:
Mum: Come here, let me look at your team.
...There. Right as rain.
p.tv: The TV: "...Vanguard Energy: Power without price."
p.stair.jensen.1:
Fru Jensen: Your friends are making a racket in the
courtyard. In my day we had manners. And bicycles.
p.stair.jensen.2: Fru Jensen: Well, we still have bicycles.
p.stair.jensen.daily:
Fru Jensen: Here, I found this in the stairwell.
It's not mine. Probably.
p.yard.lukas.1:
Lukas: Ninety-nine point nine percent grid uptime!
Vanguard's numbers are perfect this quarter.
p.yard.maja.1:
Maja: Perfect numbers are the ones I trust least.
Pass me that spanner?
p.yard.lukas.2:
Lukas: {player}! The Professor's giving out Pokémon
today. Five of them. Statistically, one is the best.
p.yard.maja.2:
Maja: Statistically, you're unbearable.
Come on, {player}. Last one to the Palm House
is a Magikarp.
p.bridge.sign:
Sign: Dronning Louises Bro. Busiest bike bridge
in the world. Keep right. Signal.
Don't stop in the lane.
p.bridge.tut.1: Commuters ride across in waves. Wait for a gap, then cross.
p.bridge.billboard: Billboard: VANGUARD ENERGY. Power without price.
p.bridge.maja:
Maja: Everything has a price. Somebody's just
not telling us who pays it.
p.r1.sign: Route 1: Søerne Path. ↑ Nørrebro ↓ Botanical Garden
p.r1.grass: Tall grass rustles. Without a Pokémon, it's wiser to stay on the path.
p.r1.mads.1:
Cyclist Mads: Whoa! Walking in the bike lane?!
Rule one: stay right. Rule two: signal before you stop.
p.r1.mads.2:
Mads: Rule three: get a Pokémon, then come back
and I'll teach you rule four. With a battle.
p.palm.door: The Palm House. Warm, wet air drifts out the door.
p.palm.maja:
Maja: Built in 1874. Prettiest building in the city.
Don't tell Lukas I said something nice.
p.orsted.1:
Professor Ørsted: Ah! The three of you! Up here,
on the catwalk. Mind the Bounsweet, she sprays.
p.orsted.2:
Ørsted: I study Bio-Resonance: how Pokémon
and a city can hum together. Like a song.
Like a... where was I?
p.orsted.3:
Ørsted: Pokémon! Yes. Five colleagues who'd like
to see the city. Each one fits a part of it.
p.orsted.grass:
Ørsted: This one guards the King's Garden hedges.
A Grass-type. Very proper. Very serious about naps.
p.orsted.fire:
Ørsted: This one is warm as a Midsummer bonfire.
A Fire-type. Please don't let it near my ferns.
p.orsted.water:
Ørsted: This one swims the harbour baths all winter.
A Water-type. It thinks it's a seal. It's nearly right.
p.orsted.normal:
Ørsted: This one changes with the city around it.
A Normal-type. Nobody knows into what. Not even me.
p.orsted.electric:
Ørsted: And this one keeps chewing my cables.
An Electric-type. It hums like a transformer.
p.lukas.pick:
Lukas: Then I'll take {lstarter}. It has the type
advantage. Logically, it's the optimal choice.
p.lukas.pick.even:
Lukas: Nothing beats a Normal-type on paper.
So I'll take {lstarter}. Raw power. Logically.
p.maja.pick:
Maja: I'll take {mstarter}. I like the underdog.
Besides, it looked at me first.
p.orsted.dex:
Ørsted: And this: the Bio-Resonance Pokédex.
It records every Pokémon you meet.
And it hums. Don't be alarmed.
p.orsted.items:
Ørsted: Five Poké Balls and two Potions.
Weaken a wild Pokémon first, then throw.
p.lukas.challenge:
Lukas: {player}! First battle. Right here on the catwalk.
I've already run the numbers.
p.lukas.win:
Lukas: Huh. My numbers were... next time.
Next time the maths will work.
p.lukas.lose:
Lukas: As predicted. Don't feel bad,
the sample size was small.
p.orsted.heal:
Ørsted: Marvellous! Both of you. Let me patch
everyone up. There.
p.bike.1:
Ørsted: One more thing. It's a prototype.
Rotom insisted.
p.bike.2: A cargo bike with a humming box on the front. {starter} hops in.
p.bike.rotom:
Rotom: Bzzt! Ready to ride! Hold B to go faster,
press the bike button to get on!
p.coil.1:
Rotom: Bzzt! I built a Resonance Coil into the box!
It charges up while you battle. Watch the pips!
p.coil.2:
Rotom: At three pips, I can send a Current through
one move. Once per battle. Make it count!
p.coil.got:
Current unlocked! Your Coil can now charge up
and power a move with Current.
p.coil.tut: A wild Pokémon jumps out of the palms. Your Coil starts with 2 pips. Try a Current!
p.orsted.readings:
Ørsted: Langelinie readings again...
two degrees? In June? No, no, the sensor's off.
p.lukas.leave:
Lukas: I'm off to the Vanguard info centre.
They have a scholarship. See you around.
r1.jogger.intro:
Jogger Emil: Every morning, three laps of the Lakes.
And one battle. It's in the plan!
r1.jogger.line:
Emil: The swans here have right of way.
Don't argue with a swan. Ever.
r1.cyclist.intro:
Cyclist Sofie: My Pidgey and I are on a schedule.
Quick battle?
r1.cyclist.lose: Sofie: Late for work. Worth it.
r1.cyclist.line:
Sofie: Half the city bikes to work. The other
half bikes to work and complains about it.
r1.fisher.intro:
Fisher Bent: Shh. You'll scare the fish.
...There aren't any. So let's battle.
r1.fisher.lose: Bent: The fish are fine. I'm the one who's sad.
r1.fisher.line:
Bent: Forty years I've fished these lakes.
The ducks have gotten smarter. I have not.
r1.n.fisher.intro:
Fisher Ole: Night fishing is the best fishing.
Night battling is second best!
r1.n.fisher.lose: Ole: The Lotad think it's funny.
r1.n.student.intro:
Student Ida: I'm supposed to be studying.
Battling is studying. Sort of.
r1.n.student.lose: Ida: I'll tell my professor it was research.
r1.mads.challenge:
Mads: Rule four: if you've got a Pokémon,
you battle Mads! Ding ding!
r1.mads.lose:
Mads: Okay, okay. You know the lane.
Rule five: ring your bell. Always ring your bell.
r1.mads.after:
Mads: I've got eight rules in total.
Find me on other routes and I'll test you on the rest.
c1.terminal.1: A bike-lane barrier is stuck shut. A Vanguard terminal hums beside it.
c1.terminal.2: Rotom: Bzzt! Let me give it a jolt!
r1.sensor:
Man by the lake: I'm just looking at the lake.
Not at those Vanguard sensor buoys. No.
p.maja.challenge:
Maja: There you are! Lukas thinks battles are maths.
Let me show you they're stories.
p.maja.win:
Maja: Okay, that goes on the front page.
"Local kid beats zine editor."
p.maja.lose:
Maja: Front page: "Zine editor wins."
Go heal up, I'll wait. I won't, but go anyway.
p.maja.after.1:
Maja: Did you hear the Professor muttering?
Two degrees at Langelinie. In June.
p.maja.after.2:
Maja: Something in this city is off. And I'm
going to find out what. Watch this space.
p.news.1:
TV: "...harbour water at Langelinie measured
at 2°C today. Vanguard Energy says
the sensors are faulty."
p.news.2: TV: "We spoke to some visitors at the statue."
p.news.tourist:
Tourist: We came all the way from Aarhus.
And the Mermaid is so tiny!
p.mum.night:
Mum: Tiny and freezing. Lovely.
Bed, {player}. Big day tomorrow. Probably.
c1.kilen.sign: Superkilen. Red Square · Black Square · Green Park
c1.tariq.1:
Tariq: Careful, wet paint! This is the Sound.
Our mural. Every kid in the workshop did a wave.
c1.kaas.1:
Commander Kaas: Mr. Haddad. Vanguard will
install a grid relay on this wall.
It's for the public good.
c1.tariq.2:
Tariq: The public's standing right here, mate.
Ask them.
c1.tariq.3:
Tariq: Twenty-four hours. Fine. We finish it first.
But the Gym's shut today, I've got a mural to save.
c1.tariq.4:
Tariq: Go see the Professor. He rang the workshop
about his greenhouse. Something about the heating.
c1.orsted.cold:
Ørsted: My palms are shivering, {player}!
The heating's coming from the tunnels. Or it isn't.
c1.orsted.tunnels:
Ørsted: Would you look? I'd go myself, but my knees
and I have an agreement about ladders.
c1.tunnel.valve.ok: Steam hisses back into the pipe the right way.
c1.tunnel.pipe:
A copper-and-white pipe stamped VANGUARD.
It's cold, and it's pulling heat away from the Garden.
c1.eng1.intro:
Vanguard Engineer: Authorised personnel only!
You're not authorised. I can tell by your face.
c1.eng1.lose:
Engineer: This is a routine maintenance tunnel.
Routinely. Maintained.
c1.eng2.intro:
Vanguard Engineer: The pipe's working exactly as
designed. Don't ask me what it's designed to do.
c1.eng2.lose: Engineer: I just install them. I don't read the memo.
c1.swarm: Grimer pour out of a drain, drawn by the warmth!
c1.orsted.back:
Ørsted: Warm again! You're a marvel. A pipe running
backwards, you say? ...How odd. How very odd.
c1.orsted.tm:
Ørsted: Take this. TM Bullet Seed. A TM can be
used again and again. Unlike my patience for ladders.
c1.mural.tariq:
Tariq: Four colours left: green, gold, silver, purple.
Ask around Nørrebro. People here share.
c1.paint.green:
Gardener on Den Grønne Sti: Hedge-green? Take the
whole tin. Bring back the tin. And a Pidgey feather.
c1.paint.gold: Skater Yusuf: Gold? Beat me and it's yours.
c1.paint.silver:
Courier at the garage: Silver for bike frames.
Maja says you're alright. That's rare.
c1.paint.purple:
A Toxel is chewing a purple paint can in the alley.
It lets go when you offer an Oran Berry.
c1.mural.done.1: Tariq: That's it. Look at it.
c1.mural.done.2:
The mural shows a great sea creature
with its mouth open. No sound comes out.
c1.mural.done.3:
Tariq: I dreamed it. Don't ask.
Right. Gym's open. Come and get stung.
c1.gym.sign: Superkilen Gym. Leader: Tariq. "Keep the squares loud."
c1.gym.guide:
Gym guide: Hit the spray switches in the mural's
colour order and the smog vents shut. Green first!
c1.gym.wrong: Pfssht! The vents puff smog. The switches reset.
c1.gym.skater.intro: Skater: Red Square's ours. You skate or you sit.
c1.gym.muralist.intro:
Muralist: Smeargle and I painted half this wall.
Want to see the other half?
c1.gym.muralist.lose: Muralist: Okay, you can sign it. Small, in the corner.
c1.tariq.intro.1:
Tariq: This square is for the people who live here.
Not for relays. Not for anyone who wants to own it.
c1.tariq.intro.2:
Tariq: Show me you'll fight for something, {player}.
My Poison-types don't hold back.
c1.tariq.last: Tariq: Last one. Make it loud!
c1.tariq.lose: Tariq: Respect. You fight like you belong here.
c1.tariq.badge:
Tariq: This is the Spray Badge. Wear it where
people can see it.
c1.tariq.tm:
Tariq: And this: TM Acid Spray. Melts defences.
Like a good mural.
c1.tariq.bell:
Rotom: Bzzt! A bell! Ding!
Weaker wild Pokémon will scatter in bike lanes now!
c1.tariq.obey: Traded Pokémon up to Lv 25 will now obey you.
c1.lukas.1:
Lukas: Badge one. Not bad. Look what I got.
The Lindholm Scholarship. Vanguard's top programme.
c1.lukas.2:
Lukas: Director Lindholm says people like me will
keep this city running when the sea comes up.
c1.lukas.3:
Lukas: Let's see if the scholarship was a good
investment. Battle!
c1.lukas.lose: Lukas: An outlier. You're an outlier.
c1.relay: That evening the relay goes up, right over the painted sea.
c1.tariq.relay: Tariq: They didn't even wait the twenty-four hours.
c1.blackout: Click. Every light in Nørrebro goes out.
c1.roof: On the rooftop: a yellow-and-black oilskin. Then nothing.
c1.mum.dark:
Mum: Candles are in the drawer. This city, honestly.
A hundred percent clean energy and no lights.
c2.strog.sign:
Strøget. One of Europe's longest shopping streets.
Bikes walked, please.
c2.torv.stall.1:
Stall owner: Smørrebrød! Rye bread, spread, topping.
Three layers. Never two. Never four.
c2.torv.stall.2:
Stall owner: Here, a free recipe card. The Hafnian way.
Collect them and you'll eat like a king.
c2.rund.tycho:
Astronomer: The Round Tower is closed for
"routine maintenance". Go and look at something else.
c2.rund.tycho.2: Astronomer: Not the sky. The sky is mine today.
c2.busker.intro:
Busker Viggo: Every song needs an audience.
You'll do. Battle!
c2.busker.lose:
Viggo: Bravo. Take this, TM Round.
A song sounds better when everyone joins in.
c2.busker.line:
Viggo: Funny. The old fishermen's songs are all about
something in the water singing back.
c2.tourist.intro:
Tourist Gerd: We're from Aarhus! Battle us,
then tell us where the Mermaid is.
c2.tourist.lose: Gerd: Langelinie, you say? We'll go tomorrow.
c2.guard.intro:
Royal Guard Frederik: I am on duty.
I am also on lunch. Battle me quickly.
c2.guard.lose: Frederik: Back to standing very still.
c2.student.intro:
Student Anders: My thesis is on Psychic types
in urban spaces. Help me with the data?
c2.ny.sign: Nyhavn. The old harbour. Mind the cobbles.
c2.ny.maja.1:
Maja: {player}! You're here too? I got a tip
something's going down by the canal. Look!
c2.ny.boom:
BOOM. A Vanguard buoy in the canal pops like a cork.
Water everywhere.
c2.ny.freja.1: Woman in oilskin: Listen to the water!
c2.ny.deck.1: Deckhand: Nobody follows the Captain. Nobody!
c2.ny.deck.2: Deckhand: Two of you? Fine. Two of us.
c2.ny.maja.2: Maja: You and me, {player}. I'll take the left one.
c2.ny.maja.3:
Maja: Black Fleet. Yellow-and-black oilskins.
Same as the rooftop in Nørrebro.
c2.ny.maja.4:
Maja: They're headed for Refshaleøen.
The harbour bus goes there. Come on!
c2.ny.sailor.line:
Sailor Henning: Sixty years I've sailed out of Nyhavn.
Never seen the harbour this cold. Never.
c2.ny.tourist.line:
Tourist Hans-Peter: We finally saw the Mermaid.
She's so tiny! Gerd cried. From the cold.
c2.bus.bodil.1:
Captain Bodil: All aboard the harbour bus! Next stop,
Refshaleøen. Hold on to your hats. And your Pokémon.
c2.bus.bodil.2:
Bodil: Feel that chill off the water? Twenty years
I've driven this boat. It's never been like this.
c2.dock.sign: Refshaleøen. Former shipyard. Keep out. (Nobody does.)
c2.dock.crane: A crane console. Move the hook? ← → to slide, A to drop.
c2.dock.crane.ok: The container lands with a CLANG. A path opens.
c2.dock.deck.intro:
Deckhand: The sea is in pain, and you're
helping the ones who hurt it!
c2.dock.deck.lose: Deckhand: You don't even know what you're fighting for.
c2.ivar.1:
Bosun Ivar: That's far enough, kid. I built ships
in this yard for thirty years. Then they closed it.
c2.ivar.2: Ivar: Nobody closes this one. Hup!
c2.ivar.lose:
Ivar: Hah! Strong arms. Strong heart, too.
Go on, then. The Captain wants a word.
c2.freja.1: Captain Freja: So. You're the one who keeps turning up.
c2.freja.2:
Freja: I could keep you here. I won't.
I'm not the one hurting this city.
c2.freja.3:
Freja: The water at Langelinie is freezing.
Ask yourself why the company that heats
your flat doesn't care.
c2.freja.4: She drops a yellowed page as she leaves.
c2.log.1:
The Lighthouse Log, page 1: "June 1961. Trekroner.
The singing was faint tonight. I hope it's the wind."
c2.log.got: {player} found a page of the Lighthouse Log! (1/10)
c2.nail.1:
Bosun Ivar: Here. Captain said to give you this.
A copper hull nail from the old ships.
c2.nail.2:
Ivar: Copper sheathing kept the worms off the hulls.
Kept the ships whole. Maybe it'll do the same for you.
c2.nail.3:
Rotom: Bzzt! Copper! I can make Patina armour
with this! Tougher hide, but it seals
the held item.
c2.enforcer.overcharge: The Enforcer's Rotom crackles red: Overcharge! (first Vanguard use)
c2.chr.maja.1:
Maja: Welcome to my favourite part of the city.
Don't run, don't take photos of people.
Photos of Pokémon, fine.
c2.night.market: The Freetown night market: fairy lights, stalls, music.
c2.knud.1:
Old Knud: You look hungry. Everybody looks hungry.
Sit. Eat. Have I told you about the eel of '79?
c2.knud.2:
Knud: Three layers. Rye, butter, herring.
...When there's herring. There hasn't been much.
c2.knud.rod:
Knud: Here. My old rod. The lakes still have fish,
even if the harbour forgets.
c2.overhear.1:
Deckhand: Alva's keeping the boats
safe. Nobody checks the houseboats.
c2.overhear.2: Maja: ...Didn't hear that. Neither did you.
c2.orsted.scan:
Ørsted: {player}! I've sent your
Pokédex an update. It hums near hidden things now!
c2.scan.got: The Pokédex learned the Bio-Resonance scan!
c2.alva.1:
Alva: Careful on the planks. The moat's choking.
Algae everywhere, and it's June.
Too warm here, freezing there.
c2.alva.2:
Alva: Warm water from those pipes. Vanguard's
outflow. Can you help my barges?
Push the floating booms together.
c2.alva.done:
Alva: You've a knack for boats. Come by the Gym.
I'll give you a proper test.
c2.gym.sign: Stadsgraven Gym. Leader: Alva. "Swimmable for every child."
c2.gym.guide:
Gym guide: Rotate the solar mirrors on the houseboat
roofs. Sun on a lily makes it bloom into a bridge.
c2.gym.gardener.intro:
Gardener: Plants grow toward light.
So do challengers. Battle!
c2.gym.christ.intro:
Christianite: Peace, love and Petilil.
Mostly Petilil.
c2.alva.intro.1:
Alva: The canals were filthy when I was a girl.
Now kids swim in them. That took twenty years.
c2.alva.intro.2:
Alva: I don't give up on things that take time.
Neither should you.
c2.alva.badge:
Alva: The Lily Badge. And TM Magical Leaf.
It never misses. Neither do the weeds.
c2.alva.net:
Rotom: Bzzt! A Basket Net! Ride past hedges
to pick berries and items!
c2.alva.obey: Traded Pokémon up to Lv 30 will now obey you.
c2.alva.secret:
Alva: If anyone asks about my houseboats...
they're just houseboats.
c2.dusk.1: Dusk. The streetlights on the bridge flicker... and die.
c2.dusk.freja.1:
Freja: Don't be scared of the dark.
Be scared of what keeps the lights on.
c2.dusk.freja.2:
Freja: Ask Vanguard what's screaming underneath
the harbour every time you turn on the lights.
c2.dusk.freja.3: Freja: Let's see if you're worth telling.
c2.freja.win: Freja: Not yet, then. But you will be.
c2.dusk.lukas.2:
Lukas: She's a terrorist. She blacked out half the
city. And you were just... talking to her?
c2.dusk.lukas.3: Lukas: You're helping her. Battle me. Now.
c2.lukas2.lose: Lukas: This isn't over. The data's on my side.
c2.lukas2.win: Lukas: See? Vanguard keeps people safe. That's the point.
c2.dusk.maja.1: Maja picks a folded note off the rail and pockets it.
c2.dusk.maja.2:
Maja: Come on. Let's go home before the lights
come back on and somebody asks questions.
c2.end.1:
Behind you, the lights come back on. Somewhere under
the harbour, something is still singing. Barely.
c2.end.2: Copper & Current · End of the demo. Thank you for playing!
c2.end.3:
Your save is kept. The story continues in Chapter 3:
The White Butchery.
c2.end.next:
Your Pokédex buzzes. Maja:
"Kasper's food bank in Kødbyen needs hands. Take
Den Grønne Sti west out of Nørrebro. I'll find you."
c3.gate.closed:
A barrier: DEN GRØNNE STI CLOSED FOR
VANGUARD CABLE WORKS. Not today, then.
c3.r2.sign:
ROUTE 2 · DEN GRØNNE STI
Nørrebro → Frederiksberg → Vesterbro.
Bikes have right of way. Always.
c3.r2.overpass:
The overpass hums. A Vanguard cable runs along
its underside, warm to the touch.
c3.r2.cyclist.intro:
Cyclist: Fifteen kilometres before breakfast!
Keep up!
c3.r2.jogger.intro: Jogger: You're on MY lane. Battle for it!
c3.r2.jogger.lose: Jogger: Fine. It's a shared lane.
c3.r2.student.intro:
Student: I study Pokémon ecology. You'll be
my fieldwork.
c3.r2.student.lose: Student: Note to self: the fieldwork bites.
c3.r2.picker:
Berry picker: The hedges here are full of berries
in summer. Take a few, they grow back.
c3.vb.arrive:
Vesterbro. Red-brick courtyards, laundry lines,
and roasting coffee on every corner.
c3.vb.maja.1:
Maja: There you are! Kasper's kitchen in Kødbyen
is feeding two hundred people tonight.
c3.vb.maja.2:
Maja: Except the harbour fish are gone. Again.
Nobody official wants to say why.
c3.vb.maja.3:
Maja: Go and help him. He's horrible, but the
food's for real. I've got a... delivery. Later!
c3.vb.tourist:
Tourist: I biked all the way out to see the
Little Mermaid. She's smaller than my bike.
c3.vb.kid:
Kid: The café does cocoa with whipped cream
and the Pokémon get to sit by the stove!
c3.vb.oldman:
Old man: Istedgade runs east to Cykelslangen,
the orange bridge. Windy up there. Always is.
c3.cafe.1:
Barista: Welcome to Kaffebaren! Sit, stay, get
warm. That's hygge. Your Pokémon feel it too.
c3.cafe.ask: Barista: Cocoa by the stove? On the house.
c3.cafe.rest:
Your team curls up by the stove.
Everyone feels cosy and rested.
c3.cafe.no: Barista: The stove's not going anywhere.
c3.cafe.2:
Barista: There are cafés like this all over the
city. Come in whenever the weather turns.
c3.kb.arrive:
Kødbyen, the old Meatpacking District.
White tiles, neon signs and the best kitchens in Hafnia.
c3.kb.gym.closed:
A note on the Cold Stores door:
GYM CLOSED UNTIL DINNER IS SERVED. – K.
c3.kit.1:
Kasper: Is THIS a fish stock? It's warm water with
a rumour of fish in it. Again!
c3.kit.2:
Line cook Ali: Chef, there's no fish. The boats
came back empty. Third day running.
c3.kit.3:
Kasper: You. Trainer. You have legs and a bike.
Do you have a stomach for work?
c3.kit.4:
Kasper: Two hundred people eat here tonight and the
harbour gave me nothing. So: the Empty-Sea Dinner.
c3.kit.5:
Kasper: Sea buckthorn from the Kalvebod edge.
Mussels from the harbour bath at Islands Brygge.
c3.kit.6:
Kasper: And my smoked-ice salt, in my locker on the
row outside. I lost the key. Improvise.
c3.kit.7:
Kasper: Islands Brygge is over Cykelslangen, east
along Istedgade. Go. Why are you still here?
c3.kit.wait: Kasper: Buckthorn, mussels, salt. I'm counting.
c3.kit.ali:
Line cook Ali: He's not always like this.
...He's mostly like this.
c3.kit.sofie:
Line cook Sofie: Chef's locker is the one that
hums. He keeps a little cooler in it. Don't ask.
c3.locker.1: A locker. Inside: one sock, frozen solid.
c3.locker.2:
A locker. Somebody's lunch from 2019.
Close it. Close it now.
c3.locker.3: A locker. Empty apart from a cold draught.
c3.locker.4: A locker. A note: "Kasper is a genius." – Kasper
c3.locker.5: A locker. A neat stack of clean aprons.
c3.locker.hum: Bzzz... This locker hums. Frost seals the door.
c3.locker.open:
You brace a foot on the wall and pull.
The frost cracks and the door swings open!
c3.ib.arrive:
Islands Brygge. Lawns, grain silos turned into flats,
and the harbour bath, empty in June.
c3.ib.guard:
Lifeguard: The bath's shut. The water's two degrees
in June. Nobody swims, so the mussels love it.
c3.ib.guard.2:
Lifeguard: Want mussels? The pier ladder's covered.
Mind the winter bathers. They bite. Battle, I mean.
c3.ib.swim1.intro:
Winter bather: Two degrees? That's practically
a sauna!
c3.ib.swim1.lose: Winter bather: Brr. Okay. Now I'm cold.
c3.ib.swim2.intro:
Winter bather: We swim every morning. In ice.
Fear nothing!
c3.ib.swim2.lose: Winter bather: I fear you a little.
c3.ib.ladder:
Mussels cling to the old pier ladder.
You fill a net bag.
c3.got.mussels: {player} got a bag of harbour mussels!
c3.ib.bush:
A sea buckthorn bush, heavy with orange berries.
Ow, thorns. You pick a bagful anyway.
c3.got.buckthorn: {player} got a bag of sea buckthorn!
c3.ib.wilds:
KALVEBOD WILDS. Past the reeds it's open water.
(A bike with Hydrofoils could cross.)
c3.ib.ranger:
Ranger: Kalvebod's a whole wild area out there.
Tauros, Mudbray, birds you've never seen.
c3.kit.back.1:
Kasper: Mussels. Buckthorn. Salt. ...Fine. Fine!
Everyone, stations! Ali, the stock. Sofie, plates!
c3.kit.back.2:
The kitchen roars for an hour.
Two hundred plates go out of the door.
c3.kit.child.1:
Child: Chef? This is the best dinner I ever had.
My mum says thank you too.
c3.kit.child.2:
Kasper: ...It was the buckthorn.
And the team. The team did good.
c3.kit.ali.2: Line cook Ali: Did Chef just say "good"?
c3.kit.back.3:
Kasper: The Cold Stores are open. Come and lose
to me properly, {player}.
c3.kit.night: By the time you step outside, the neon's on.
c3.kit.after:
Kasper: The Cold Stores. I'm not going to wait
all night. Well. I am. But I don't like it.
c3.dj.1:
DJ Signe: Neon Nights! Tag battles, two on two,
every night. You need a partner? I've got decks.
c3.dj.ask: DJ Signe: Three rounds back to back. Ready?
c3.dj.break: DJ Signe: Water break! Your team's topped up.
c3.dj.done:
DJ Signe: That's the set! You were tight.
Take these, the house always pays.
c3.dj.after: DJ Signe: Come back any night. The beat goes on.
c3.dj.day:
DJ Signe: Come back after dark. Neon doesn't
work in daylight, it's science.
c3.raver.1: Raver Kim: The bass drop is a lifestyle.
c3.raver.2: Raver Lou: Kødbyen never sleeps. Neither do we.
c3.gym.sign:
KASPER'S MENU: FORRET · HOVEDRET · DESSERT.
Steam goes in that order. Always. – K.
c3.gym.guide:
Gym guide: Ice floors! Once you slide, you don't
stop till you hit something. Plan your route!
c3.valve.ok: Pssshhh! Steam rushes into the pipes.
c3.valve.wrong:
Hissss... the valves slam shut. Wrong course!
(Every valve is closed again.)
c3.valve.melt:
Steam roars through the pipes. The ice block
in the gap groans, cracks... and melts away!
c3.gym.mette.intro:
Sous-chef Mette: Chef says if you can't take the cold,
get out of the kitchen.
c3.gym.mette.lose: Sous-chef Mette: I'm out of the kitchen.
c3.gym.rasmus.intro:
Commis Rasmus: First week on the job. Don't tell Chef
I'm nervous.
c3.gym.rasmus.lose: Commis Rasmus: He's going to know.
c3.kasper.intro.1:
Kasper: Cold is honest. It keeps what's good and
it kills what isn't.
c3.kasper.intro.2:
Kasper: You fed my district today.
Now let's see if you can take the heat. The cold. Whatever.
c3.kasper.lose:
Kasper: Hm. Seasoned well. Plated well.
The Frost Badge is yours.
c3.kasper.win: Kasper: Undercooked. Come back when you're done.
c3.kasper.tm:
Kasper: And TM Icy Wind. It slows them down,
so you can think. I always need to think.
c3.kasper.bike:
Kasper: This crate came from the Palm House for you.
Ørsted says your bike is overdue an upgrade.
c3.got.bike: {player} got the Bike Lamp and the Hydrofoils!
c3.kasper.bike.2:
The Lamp lights the bike at night, and the Hydrofoils
let it skim calm water. Kalvebod Wilds is open!
c3.kasper.after:
Kasper: The harbour fish will come back. They'd better.
I've got a menu to write.
c3.maja.text:
Your Pokédex buzzes. Maja:
"Cykelslangen. Now. Race you over."
c3.maja.1:
Maja: Took you long enough! First one over buys
the cardamom buns.
c3.maja.2:
Maja: And the tailwind's on my side today.
Battle first, though. Loser rides behind.
c3.maja.win: Maja: Ha! Cardamom buns are on you.
c3.maja.3:
Maja: ...Okay. Truth time. The relay buoy in Nyhavn?
The drydock? Freja knew because I told her.
c3.maja.4:
Maja: I've been feeding the Black Fleet tips.
Where Vanguard's crews are. What they're digging.
c3.maja.5:
Maja: I want the truth. They're the only ones
looking for it. Everyone else just reads the brochure.
c3.maja.6:
Maja: Don't tell Lukas. He'd hand me to the
Enforcers and call it a good day's work.
c3.maja.7: Maja waves and rides off into the wind.
c3.orsted.2:
Ørsted: {player}! The Palm House's resonance sensors
picked up something under the city. A rhythm.
c3.orsted.3:
Ørsted: Almost like... no. Never mind.
Come by when you can.
c3.end:
Your save is kept. Head home to Nørrebro for
Chapter 4: Lanterns Out.
c4.start.1:
Your Pokédex buzzes. A message from Tariq:
"Back in Nørrebro? Good. Something's wrong at Assistens."
c4.start.2:
Tariq: "Søren's lanterns went dark last night. All of them.
The kids on my street are scared to walk home."
c4.start.3:
Tariq: "Søren's asking for trainers. The cemetery's
straight up the lane, north of the Pokémon Center."
c4.gate.early:
The lane to Assistens is lined with candles.
A card reads: CLOSED FOR THE LANTERN FESTIVAL. Soon.
c4.as.arrive:
Assistens Kirkegård. Old trees, mossy headstones
and long shadows. People picnic here by day.
c4.soren.1:
Søren: You came. Tariq said you might.
I'm Søren. I keep the Lantern Walk.
c4.soren.2:
Søren: Every night for twenty years, Litwick have
lit these lanterns. They like the company.
c4.soren.3:
Søren: Three nights ago they started leaving.
Last night the last lantern went out.
c4.soren.4:
Søren: Grief, I understand. But Litwick don't flee
from grief. They flee from cold.
c4.soren.litwick: ...! A Litwick! It's shaking. Look how dim it is.
c4.soren.5:
Søren: The storm drain. It went into the storm drain.
Could you... follow it? I'm not much good underground.
c4.soren.6:
Søren: I'm not much good anywhere, some days.
I'll keep the lanterns company until you're back.
c4.soren.wait:
Søren: The grate is in the east corner, past the
last row of graves. Please. Mind the cold.
c4.grate:
A rusty storm-drain grate. Cold air breathes
up through the bars.
c4.grate.ask: Climb down into the storm drain?
c4.as.picnic1:
Picnicker: We come here every Sunday. It's the
quietest park in the city. Nobody minds.
c4.as.picnic2:
Picnicker: Kierkegaard's buried here! And H.C. Andersen.
And my grandad, who'd want you to know he was taller.
c4.as.ghost1.intro:
Ghost Hunter: The lanterns are out and the ghosts
are restless. Perfect conditions!
c4.as.ghost1.lose: Ghost Hunter: I think I need a lantern of my own.
c4.as.ghost2.intro:
Ghost Hunter: Shh. Did you feel that? A cold spot!
...Oh, it's you. Battle me anyway.
c4.as.ghost2.lose: Ghost Hunter: Spooked. By a person. Embarrassing.
c4.as.picnic.intro:
Picnicker: A battle before the cake?
Fine, but quickly.
c4.as.picnic.lose: Picnicker: Now I need the cake.
c4.grave: Weathered letters. Someone has left fresh flowers.
c4.lantern.out: An iron lantern on a post. Cold and dark.
c4.lantern.lit:
An iron lantern. A Litwick dozes inside it,
glowing softly.
c4.sd.arrive:
The storm drain. Water drips somewhere ahead,
and your breath is fogging. In June.
c4.sd.ladder: The ladder back up to Assistens.
c4.sd.eng1.intro:
Vanguard Engineer: Whoa, civilians can't be down here.
This is routine maintenance! Routine!
c4.sd.eng1.lose:
Engineer: Look, the water table's dropping. It does that.
Sometimes. Lately. A lot.
c4.sd.eng2.intro:
Vanguard Engineer: Did my colleague let you past?
Typical. Fine. Battle!
c4.sd.eng2.lose:
Engineer: Don't touch the intake. Seriously.
It's colder than the inside of a freezer.
c4.sd.ice:
The sump has frozen over. The groundwater is
sinking away, and freezing as it goes.
c4.sd.pipe:
A huge iron pipe, rimed with frost. Stencilled:
VANGUARD · HAVNESTRØM 3 · INTAKE.
c4.sd.pipe.2:
Water is being pulled into it, hard.
It's flowing toward the harbour.
c4.sd.huddle:
The Litwick from the cemetery are here, huddled
together around one bigger flame.
c4.sd.lampent:
The Lampent flares! It's frightened, and it's
pulling the Litwick's warmth into itself!
c4.sd.after.1:
The Lampent's flame steadies. The Litwick stop
shivering and drift toward the ladder.
c4.sd.after.2:
They want to go home. Something down here is
pulling the water, and the cold, toward the harbour.
c4.sd.up: A maintenance ladder leads up toward the cemetery.
c4.relit.1:
The Litwick float up out of the grate, one by one,
and settle into the lanterns. Night falls.
c4.relit.2:
Søren: Oh. Oh, look at them.
You brought them home.
c4.relit.3:
Søren: A pipe pulling the water toward the harbour...
Vanguard's pipe. I'll write it down. I write everything down.
c4.relit.4:
Søren: The Lantern Walk is lit again. That means
my gym is open. Tonight, while it's dark.
c4.relit.5:
Søren: The gate is at the top of the avenue.
Read the stones. The dead are good with directions.
c4.walk.locked:
The Lantern Walk gate is chained shut.
Søren keeps the key.
c4.walk.night:
Søren's sign: THE LANTERN WALK IS LIT
FROM NIGHTFALL UNTIL DAWN.
c4.walk.waited:
You sit on a bench under the lime trees.
The lanterns flicker on, one by one.
c4.gym.sign:
THE LANTERN WALK · Leader: Søren
"Speak your grief. Then walk on."
c4.gym.guide:
Gym guide: Three hedges, three gaps each. Only one
gap is true. The rhymes on the stones tell you which.
c4.gym.guide.2:
Gym guide: Go through a false one and the wind
blows your lantern out. Back to the start you go.
c4.rhyme.1:
A stone, carved with a rhyme:
"The match girl warmed her frozen hand
c4.rhyme.1b:
where the sun goes down upon the land."
...The sun goes down in the west.
c4.rhyme.2:
A stone, carved with a rhyme:
"The ugly duckling, grey and slow,
c4.rhyme.2b:
flew home toward the morning's glow."
...The morning glows in the east.
c4.rhyme.3:
A stone, carved with a rhyme:
"The steadfast soldier would not bend;
c4.rhyme.3b: go straight ahead until the end."
c4.gust:
Whoosh! A gust of wind snuffs out your lantern!
In the dark, the paths twist around you...
c4.gust.back: ...and you're back where the walk began.
c4.gym.medium1.intro:
Medium: The wind whispers to me. It whispers
"this one's going to lose."
c4.gym.medium2.intro:
Medium: I've walked this path a thousand times.
Never once in the right order.
c4.gym.medium2.lose: Medium: You read the stones. Clever.
c4.soren.gym.1:
Søren: You found him. Hans Christian Andersen.
He wrote about little things that suffered quietly.
c4.soren.gym.2:
Søren: Mermaids. Match girls. Tin soldiers.
I always thought he understood ghosts.
c4.soren.gym.3:
Søren: I've been sad for a long time. It made me
still. You made me move tonight. So: let's battle.
c4.soren.lose:
Søren: Ah. The lantern burns brighter for being
shared. Take this. The Lantern Badge.
c4.soren.win:
Søren: Grief isn't a reason to stop.
Walk the path again when you're ready.
c4.soren.tm:
Søren: And Hex. It hurts more when the target's
already hurting. Use it kindly, if you can.
c4.soren.verse.1:
Søren: One more thing. When the lanterns went out,
I saw words on the back of Andersen's stone.
c4.soren.verse.2:
Søren: Words that weren't there before. Or that
only show in the dark. I copied them for you.
c4.verse:
"Where the king's water sleeps beneath the hill,
the mermaid's price is written still."
c4.soren.verse.3:
Søren: The king's water. The mermaid.
I think Ørsted should hear this.
c4.tremor.1:
...! The ground lurches! The lanterns swing
and the Litwick flare in fright!
c4.tremor.2:
Your Pokédex buzzes: a news alert.
"TREMOR SHAKES COPENHAGEN. RUNDETÅRN'S RAMP CRACKED."
c4.tremor.3:
Søren: Copenhagen doesn't have earthquakes.
...Go. Find Ørsted.
c4.end:
Step back out into Assistens to begin
Chapter 5: The Cisterns.
c4.soren.after:
Søren: The Litwick are staying. I asked them.
Come and walk with us any night.
c4.gs.day:
A headstone, older than the others. Something
about it feels like it's waiting for dark.
c4.gs.1:
KAREN · 1840–1859 · "She danced until her shoes
wore through." Music drifts from nowhere...
c4.gs.2:
BUSTER · faithful dog of the night watchman
"He's still waiting by the gate." A low howl...
c4.gs.3:
OLE · who sold umbrellas and told bedtime stories.
"Sleep tight." Something yawns in the dark...
c4.gs.4:
PERNILLE · Tea shop, Nørrebrogade, 1901–1958.
"Kettle's on." A cup rattles on the stone...
c4.gs.5:
THE LAMPLIGHTER OF ASSISTENS · 1890–1951
"He kept the lights on." A small flame flickers...
c4.gs.rise: A ghost rises from the grave!
c4.gs.calm: The ghost fades, at peace. You remember its story.
c4.gs.soren.hint:
Søren: There are five old graves here with stories
that wake at night. If you hear them all, tell me.
c4.gs.soren.progress:
Søren: You've heard {n} of the five stories.
The rest only wake after dark.
c4.gs.soren.done:
Søren: All five. You listened to all of them.
Here: you've earned these. And my poem book.
c4.gs.got:
{player} received a Dusk Stone, a Reaper Cloth
and Søren's Poem Book!
c4.bk.closed:
Baker: Morning! Well, almost. We do our real
baking before the city wakes up.
c4.bk.1:
Baker Birthe: My delivery boy's moved to Aarhus and
six customers want their kanelsnegle before eight.
c4.bk.2:
Baker Birthe: You've got a bike. Six swirls, six
letterboxes. Before the city wakes. Interested?
c4.bk.ask: Help Birthe with the dawn deliveries?
c4.bk.late:
Baker Birthe: Not now, it's too late in the day.
Come back between dawn and breakfast.
c4.bk.wait: Wait in the bakery until dawn?
c4.bk.waited:
You nap on a flour sack. When you wake,
the ovens are roaring and it's barely light.
c4.bk.go:
Baker Birthe: Red letterboxes: two in Vesterbro,
two in Kødbyen, two in Nørrebro. Go, go!
c4.bk.progress:
Baker Birthe: {n} delivered! The rest before breakfast,
please. They don't taste the same at lunch.
c4.bk.done.1:
Baker Birthe: All six! Before eight!
You're faster than the boy ever was.
c4.bk.done.2:
Baker Birthe: Here. This Egg turned up in the dough
proofer. I think it likes it warm.
c4.bk.got.egg: {player} received an Egg and an Exp. Candy M!
c4.bk.after:
Baker Birthe: The Egg was in the dough.
I'm not asking questions.
c4.mb: A red letterbox with a brass flap.
c4.mb.late:
Curtains are open and the street's awake.
Deliveries are for before breakfast.
c4.mb.put:
You slip a warm kanelsnegl through the flap.
Delivered!
c4.mb.done: You already delivered here. It smells of cinnamon.
c4.mb.last: That's the last one! Back to Birthe's bakery.
c5.start.1:
Your Pokédex hasn't stopped buzzing since the tremor.
Forty-one messages. One of them is Ørsted.
c5.start.2:
Ørsted: "That tremor. Hafnia sits on chalk, and chalk
doesn't shake. Something underneath is moving."
c5.start.3:
Ørsted: "Meet me at the glass pyramid in Søndermarken.
Den Grønne Sti, up the overpass stairs. Bring the verse!"
c5.gate.early:
The overpass stairs are taped off.
VANGUARD CABLE WORKS. THANK YOU FOR YOUR PATIENCE.
c5.fb.arrive:
Frederiksberg. Lime-tree avenues, the yellow palace
on its hill, and the zoo's elephants trumpeting.
c5.brief.1:
Ørsted: There you are! Søren read me your verse over
the phone. "Where the king's water sleeps beneath the hill."
c5.brief.2:
Ørsted: The king's water! The old royal reservoir
under Søndermarken. The Cisterns. It has to be.
c5.brief.lukas.1:
Lukas: Professor, it's a poem. Vanguard's seismic team
says the tremor was a settling pipe. 94% confidence.
c5.brief.maja.1:
Maja: Vanguard's team also says the harbour is
"basically drinkable". I brought a torch.
c5.brief.3:
Ørsted: The Cisterns are a gallery now. Concerts, art,
that sort of thing. But below the gallery floor...
c5.brief.4:
Ørsted: ...is the part nobody visits. My grandfather
swore there were rooms down there older than the city.
c5.brief.lukas.2:
Lukas: Fine. I'm coming so someone measures
something. Somebody has to be the adult.
c5.brief.maja.2: Maja: Last one down is a Vanguard press release!
c5.brief.5:
Ørsted: Maja, wait for... and she's gone. Splendid.
The pyramid's on the park side. See you below!
c5.brief.6: They head off toward the glass pyramid in Søndermarken.
c5.fb.sign:
FREDERIKSBERG
Frederiksberg Allé ↑ Palace · Søndermarken →
Den Grønne Sti ↓
c5.fb.palace:
FREDERIKSBERG PALACE
Royal Danish Cadet Academy. Visitors by appointment.
c5.fb.pyramid:
CISTERNERNE
The old royal reservoir. Gallery closed today:
VANGUARD SURVEY IN PROGRESS.
c5.fb.zoo:
KØBENHAVNS ZOO
Staff entrance. Night keeper on duty from dusk.
c5.fb.surveyor:
Vanguard Surveyor: Scanning for structural anomalies.
Nothing to see. Please don't look at the drones.
c5.fb.oldman:
Old man: My father took me down to the Cisterns once,
back when they still held water. Black as ink.
c5.fb.oldman.2:
Old man: He dropped a coin in and we never heard
it land. He said the water was listening.
c5.pyramid.locked:
The pyramid's glass door is locked.
A Vanguard notice: SURVEY IN PROGRESS.
c5.fb.cadet1.intro:
Cadet: Halt! Civilians on the palace lawn
must submit to inspection. By battle!
c5.fb.cadet2.intro:
Cadet: We drill at dawn and battle at noon.
You're early. Or late. Either way: battle!
c5.fb.cadet2.lose: Cadet: I'll be doing extra laps for that.
c5.fb.jogger.intro:
Jogger: Third lap of Søndermarken!
Keep up if you can!
c5.fb.jogger.lose: Jogger: I'm walking the fourth lap.
c5.fb.picnic.intro:
Picnicker: The deer here eat out of your hand.
My Pokémon eat out of my basket. Battle?
c5.fb.picnic.lose: Picnicker: At least the sandwiches survived.
c5.cis.arrive:
The stairs go down, and down, and the daylight
gives up. Water drips somewhere in the dark.
c5.cis.1:
Ørsted: Marvellous! Feel that air, cold as
a cellar. Your lamp won't reach far down here.
c5.cis.2:
Ørsted: Maja ran on ahead, of course. Lukas and I will
take the dry gallery round the side. You take the halls.
c5.cis.lukas:
Lukas: My scanner says there's nothing past this hall.
A solid wall. ...My scanner has never been wrong.
c5.cis.3:
Ørsted: Then the wall is where we start! Look for still
water. Old builders liked their mirrors.
c5.cis.4:
Ørsted: We'll meet in the middle. Shout if you see
anything with teeth.
c5.cis.up: Stone stairs lead back up to the pyramid. Climb up?
c5.cis.explorer.intro:
Explorer: You're not with Vanguard? Good. They
chased me out of the north hall. Battle to warm up?
c5.cis.explorer.lose:
Explorer: The drones are scanning the walls, not the
floor. Whatever they want is behind the stone.
c5.pool.1:
A still, round pool. You lean over it.
In the reflection, the hall behind you looks different.
c5.pool.2:
Where the east wall stands, the reflection shows
an arch, and a passage beyond it.
c5.pool.sableye:
...! Two gem eyes glint in the dark! The wall was
an illusion, and its maker doesn't want to be found!
c5.pool.3:
The Sableye's trick fades. Where the wall stood,
an old brick arch opens into the dark.
c5.pool.after:
The pool is still. In the reflection, the arch is
exactly where it is.
c5.wall:
Cold, wet stone. ...Or is it? It looks
a little too smooth.
c5.flood:
Black water. You can't see the bottom.
Something long and pale moves under the surface.
c5.wheel:
A brass sluice wheel, green with age.
An arrow is stamped on it: AFLØB. Drain.
c5.wheel.1:
Gears grind in the walls. The water drops with
a long sigh, and a stone walkway surfaces!
c5.wheel.2:
Somewhere below, a sluice gate thunders open.
The reservoir drains, and a causeway rises to the south!
c5.wheel.done: The wheel is turned as far as it goes.
c5.wheel.stuck:
The wheel won't budge. The water on the other side
is pressing on the gate. Lower the level first.
c5.drone.intro:
Survey Drone: BIOLOGICAL OBSTRUCTION DETECTED.
PLEASE STAND CLEAR OF THE SCAN.
c5.drone.lose: Survey Drone: SCAN INTERRUPTED. REPORTING TO DR. BRIX.
c5.swarm.1:
A cloud of drones hangs in front of an old doorway.
Their scan beams sweep the stone, back and forth.
c5.swarm.2:
Survey Drones: ANOMALY CONFIRMED. CHAMBER SEALED.
INTRUDER WILL BE REMOVED.
c5.swarm.maja.1:
Maja: There you are! These things chased me round
three halls. They're guarding a door. Brix's drones.
c5.swarm.maja.2:
Maja: Want to find out what's behind it?
Together. On three. Three!
c5.swarm.3:
The drones spark, wobble and drop to the floor.
The old doorway stands open.
c5.swarm.maja.3:
Maja: Brix had these scanning for a room nobody
is supposed to know exists. Which means Vanguard knows.
c5.swarm.maja.4:
Maja: I'm getting pictures. Every single page.
Come on!
c5.swarm.idle: A survey drone. Its scan beam sweeps the doorway.
c5.ar.arrive:
A dry vaulted room, its shelves heavy with ledgers.
The air smells of old paper and the sea.
c5.ar.1:
Ørsted: Here you are! The dry gallery came out
behind those shelves. Look at this place...
c5.ar.maja.1:
Maja: The ledgers have a signature on every page.
H. C. Andersen. THE Andersen.
c5.ar.ledger.1:
Ørsted: "In the year 1167 the Bishop made a Pact
with the Voice of the Sound, called Langelira."
c5.ar.ledger.2:
Ørsted: "She would calm the storms and bring the herring.
The city would sing to her each Midsummer, and remember."
c5.ar.ledger.3:
Ørsted: "I have written the story as a tale of a mermaid
who trades her voice. Let them think it a fairy tale."
c5.ar.ledger.4:
Ørsted: "But a pearl of her song, the Mermaid's Tear, was
set in bronze at Langelinie, so the city could hear her."
c5.ar.maja.2:
Maja: The Little Mermaid statue? The one tourists
say is "tiny"? That's... a hearing aid for a legend?
c5.ar.schematic.1:
Pinned over the ledgers: a modern schematic. Vanguard
cables run from Langelinie straight into the statue.
c5.ar.schematic.2:
The margins are full of equations. RESONANCE CAPTURE
AT 41 Hz. DRAW: CONTINUOUS. A note: "Ørsted, 2016."
c5.ar.orsted.1:
Ørsted: ...Those are my equations. That's my paper.
Resonance capture. I wrote that.
c5.ar.confess.1:
Ørsted: Ten years ago a young director asked me
how you'd listen to a Pokémon from very far away.
c5.ar.confess.2:
Ørsted: I told him. I was flattered.
I didn't ask why.
c5.ar.confess.3:
Ørsted: And when the harbour went quiet and the herring
left, I told myself it was the climate. I chose not to look.
c5.ar.lukas.1:
Lukas: Stop. Listen to yourselves. A singing sea monster
under the harbour? This is a fairy tale. Literally.
c5.ar.lukas.2:
Lukas: Vanguard keeps the lights on for two million
people. They're not draining a mermaid. That's insane.
c5.ar.lukas.3: Lukas: I'm going. Somebody here has to stay sane.
c5.ar.maja.3:
Maja: ...I've been saying for two years that Vanguard
was hiding something. I was right.
c5.ar.maja.4: Maja: I thought being right would feel better.
c5.ar.orsted.2:
Ørsted: Take this. A copy of the Pact ledger, in Andersen's
own hand. If anyone ever asks for proof...
c5.ar.orsted.3:
Ørsted: Maja and I will photograph the rest. The back
stairs come out by the pyramid. Go after Lukas. Please.
c5.ledger.1:
A ledger in brown ink: "1167. The Bishop's Pact.
Calm seas and silver herring, for a song each Midsummer."
c5.ledger.2:
A ledger in brown ink: "Should the song ever be taken,
the sea will rise in grief." The page is water-stained.
c5.ledger.3:
A ledger in brown ink: "I hid the second ledger where
the dragons guard the money. Margrethe's people keep it."
c5.ar.exit: You climb the back stairs. Daylight, at last.
c5.lukas.1: Lukas: You came after me. Of course you did.
c5.lukas.2:
Lukas: My mum writes Vanguard's press releases. My grandad
lost his job when the shipyard closed. Vanguard rehired him.
c5.lukas.3:
Lukas: You don't get to wreck that over a bedtime story.
Battle me. If I'm wrong, prove it.
c5.lukas.lose: Lukas: ...That doesn't prove anything. It doesn't.
c5.lukas.win: Lukas: See? The numbers don't lie. People do.
c5.lukas.4: Lukas: Don't follow me this time. I need to think.
c5.after.maja.1:
Maja: He'll come round. Lukas always comes round.
Usually three weeks after he should.
c5.after.orsted.1:
Ørsted: I'm going to sit with those ledgers until I
understand what I did. All of it. I owe her that.
c5.after.maja.2:
Maja: And I'm going to print a zine nobody can ignore.
Undergrunden, special issue.
c5.after.orsted.2:
Ørsted: You need rest. And when you're ready, the
city still needs its Gym Leaders. Look up, not down.
c5.hook.1:
Your Pokédex buzzes: a news alert.
"RUNDETÅRN TO REOPEN AFTER TREMOR REPAIRS."
c5.hook.2:
"The royal astronomer, Tycho Brahe-Lund, says
the telescope is 'insulted' by the misalignment."
c5.end:
Your save is kept. The story continues in
Chapter 6: Look Up.
c5.zoo.closed:
Keeper: The zoo's closed to the public today.
Something about Vanguard cables under the paddocks.
c5.zoo.1:
Keeper: Oh, thank goodness, a trainer. Last night's tremor
shook the paddock gates open. Three of ours got out.
c5.zoo.2:
Keeper: They'll hide by day. After dark they'll come
out to graze. Could you look for them tonight?
c5.zoo.ask: Help with the zoo's night shift?
c5.zoo.wait:
Keeper: They only come out at night. Wait with me
until dark?
c5.zoo.go:
Keeper: A Phanpy, a Pancham and a Skiddo.
They know their names. Mostly.
c5.zoo.progress:
Keeper: {n} of 3 back home! The others are still
out there somewhere. Check the lawns and the palace.
c5.zoo.phanpy:
A little Phanpy, munching the park grass.
It trumpets happily and follows you.
c5.zoo.pancham:
A Pancham is chewing on a leaf like a cigar.
It squints at you, then decides you're all right.
c5.zoo.skiddo:
A Skiddo is nibbling the pyramid's flower bed.
It lets you lead it by the horns.
c5.zoo.back: You lead it back to the keeper at the zoo gate.
c5.zoo.all: That's all three! The keeper will want to thank you.
c5.zoo.done.1:
Keeper: All three home, and not a scratch on them!
You're a natural. Want a job? Kidding. Mostly.
c5.zoo.done.2:
Keeper: Take this. Our Donphan laid it last week,
and she'd want it to go to someone who cares.
c5.zoo.got: {player} got an Egg and 3 Ultra Balls!
c5.zoo.after:
Keeper: The night shift is quiet again.
Come visit the elephants. They remember you.
